validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki fetch for this row returned an empty/failed harvest this run (Cloudflare block per scope notes) and the sheet's ref cells were already all MISSING_REF, so this is entirely fresh research, not re-verification of an existing cite. Found SNGPL's own current transmission-system province-wise breakdown page (https://www.sngpl.com.pk/web/ -> Transmission System -> Province-Wise Transmission Breakup, stated 'as of 30-06-2025'). Its Sindh-province table lists a row 'QADIRPUR LINE | 30-inch | 53.13 km' -- an EXACT match to GEM's current LengthKnown=53.13/km and Diameter=30/in for P4087. The same table also independently lists 'QADIRPUR LINE | 36-inch | 53.14 km' and 'QADIRPUR LINE (LNG PHASE-II) | 42-inch | 53.14 km' immediately adjacent -- exact matches to roster siblings P4088 and P4089 respectively. This resolves the duplicate-suspicion check raised by the near-identical naming/length: these are three genuinely distinct, SNGPL-confirmed PARALLEL lines from the same Qadirpur origin (mainline + loopline + a later LNG-Phase-II capacity addition, each a separate physical pipe at a different diameter), not a relabel/segment double-count of one pipe. The page sits under SNGPL's own 'Transmission System' navigation section (not distribution/gathering), confirming PipelineType=transmission is correct -- this is a trunk line into SNGPL's core grid, not a field gathering line. Because it is SNGPL's own current network table it also directly supports Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, and Owner1=SNGPL 100% (this is literally SNGPL's own asset on SNGPL's own current-network page). CAVEAT: this is one strong primary source (the owner/operator itself), not two independent origins -- WebSearch was exhausted session-wide (200/200 budget) and general search engines (Bing/DuckDuckGo/Ecosia/Marginalia) returned garbage/unrelated content when fetched directly, and OGRA's site 403'd, so I could not reach a second, non-SNGPL corroborating source this run despite trying. Tier is therefore medium, not high, pending a second source (an OGRA State-of-Industry report or an SNGPL/OGDCL annual report PDF would be the next things to try). Wikipedia's Sui Northern Gas Pipelines and Qadirpur gas field articles were checked and do not mention this specific line.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records EndLocation=Bhong / EndState/Province=Punjab, i.e. this line is recorded as crossing from Sindh into Punjab. SNGPL's province-wise breakdown, however, lists the 53.13 km/30in 'QADIRPUR LINE' entirely inside its SINDH-province table (distinct from a separate, shorter 'QADIRPUR - AC-1X LINE' listed in the PUNJAB table at 17.11/16.88/17.13 km for the 30/36/42in lines respectively). This could simply reflect SNGPL's provincial accounting convention (attributing a cross-border line to its originating province) rather than a real error, or it could mean GEM's Bhong/Punjab endpoint actually describes what SNGPL books separately as the Punjab-side 'AC-1X' continuation. I could not resolve which with the sources available this session (search engines non-functional via WebFetch, OGRA blocked). Flagging as an open, unresolved endpoint detail rather than an affirmative error -- nothing found actively contradicts Qadirpur(Sindh)->Bhong(Punjab), but nothing directly confirms the Bhong terminus either.
